wire_restart_contract: Configure separate WorldPath and DataPath through public server.New; explicitly call public LoadWorld and LoadServerData, matching the embedding/CLI startup contract.

Keep physical chest/barrel/ender-chest/sign blocks unchanged between separate public SaveWorld and SaveServerData snapshots. World overrides are copied separately; no joint cross-store cut is promised.
Player775 receives the measured named nested shulker through creative ingress, plain inventory and ender storage, and nonzero XP fields, then retires after an initial successful public data save.

Player776 joins, receives distinct plain counts/XP plus the same measured nested stack, and completes public SaveServerData. Copy schema3 DataPath immediately before active776 disconnect or runtime stop; cached offline775 must be included.

Save a later different live source generation; restart a fresh runtime using the earlier copied artifacts. Both profiles independently inspect initial inventory, compare source-observed XP bytes, open chest/barrel/ender menus and parse the sign chunk-BE NBT.

The fixture-only slot reader accepts plain stacks and measured custom_name=6/container=75 codecs; rejects other/duplicate/removed components, malformed nesting and trailing bytes; component presence is compared, and only trailing empty container entries are normalized.
scope_limits: Schema3 and existing numeric item handles are retained; no canonical item persistence migration is implied.
Player cursor state, all generic container types, native player files, all-dimension atomic durability, fsync, power-loss survival and latency bounds are not claimed.
Existing command parsing omits nested child custom names; this slice preserves that limitation and uses measured creative ingress plus item-copy to create the named fixture.

Copied completion is observed before active teardown; this is not proof of I/O overlap. Deterministic blocked-worker tests and the separately measured responsiveness probe establish scheduling properties.

functional_race.result: pass both selected tests, no races/skips/timeouts; timings are functional-only observations
